item_identification.method: The leaf's old text names the mechanic 'Time Stop'. Grep over data/item-atoms/*.json shows exactly two items declaring behavior 'Time Stop': Zhonya's Hourglass (3157) and its component Seeker's Armguard (2420, buildsFrom of 3157). data/items.json confirms both carry the identical active text. The finding below holds identically for either, so the ambiguity is not load-bearing.

step_1_declared_families.conclusion: The new value's premise 'Every declared family on this item is a defence' is false on the cached atom declaration. The item declares the 'stats' family carrying stats.ability-power (105 AP on 3157 / 40 AP on 2420) — a purely offensive stat that feeds every Syndra ability ratio and therefore directly raises outgoing damage — and it declares the 'damage' family (damage.resistance-mitigation, related to damage-instance and both penetration atoms). Neither 'stats' nor 'damage' is a defence family; at most stats.armor and the mitigation atom are defensive, and 'every' is quantified over all of them.

step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.quote_a: Put yourself in {{tip|stasis (buff)|stasis}} for {{fd|2.5}} seconds, rendering you {{tip|untargetable}} and {{tip|invulnerable}} for the duration but also unable to move, declare [[basic attack]]s, cast [[champion ability|abilities]], use [[summoner spell]]s, or [[active ability items|activate items]].
step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.quote_b: Full disable that also makes the unit invulnerable and untargetable; cannot be cleansed, unaffected by tenacity, disables even summoner spells.
step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.derivation: Let W be the fight window the utility outcome is scored over and let s be the seconds spent in stasis (s = 0 if the active is never pressed; s = 2.5 per activation per the cached duration). The cached text is explicit that during those s seconds the holder cannot declare basic attacks and cannot cast abilities. Outgoing damage over the window is therefore evaluated on the reduced acting window W - s, not on W: TDD_out(W) = TDD_out(W - s) < TDD_out(W) for any s > 0 and any nonzero DPS. Stasis is thus an outgoing-damage-suppressing mechanic in addition to a survivability one — it is a *full disable*, self-applied.
step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.conclusion: The new value's claim that 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD' is contradicted directly by the cached wiki text: stasis suppresses the holder's own attacks and casts for its duration, which is precisely a change to outgoing TDD.

step_3_what_the_correct_reason_must_say.reasoning: Because the effect on the window is a function of s (seconds actually spent in stasis) and s is not determined by owning the item — the active is optional, self-cast, and bounded at 2.5 s per use (data/items.json 3157.active[0]) — the only sound pricing is from an explicit, bounded active-seconds scenario input. Carrying the item with s = 0 must produce zero effect on the outcome. That is exactly the old value's statement, and nothing in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md contradicts it. docs/math-foundations.md contains no identity covering utility_outcomes/focus item coverage, so it neither supports nor refutes either string; the decision rests on the cached wiki/atom evidence above.
step_3_what_the_correct_reason_must_say.computed_correct_reason: Time Stop is priced only from the explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input; item presence alone never assumes stasis.

caveats: Scenario 'syndra_derived_order_120' is not defined anywhere under data/ (data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json does not contain it), so the exact build slot at item_coverage[1] could not be confirmed from the permitted evidence tree. The item was identified from the mechanic named in the old value; both items that can produce that name yield the same verdict.

If the change under test re-ordered item_coverage so that index 1 now denotes a different item, the new string would still have to be true of that item; no item in data/item-atoms/ that carries stasis satisfies 'every declared family is a defence', and every mage-line item declares stats.ability-power, so the sentence is not rescuable by re-indexing.
verdict_rationale: The new value makes two assertions, both falsified by the cached data: (1) 'every declared family on this item is a defence' — the item declares the 'stats' family with 105 AP (offensive) and the 'damage' family; (2) 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD' — the cached Time Stop text and the stasis atom definition state the holder is fully disabled and cannot declare basic attacks or cast abilities for the 2.5 s duration, which reduces outgoing damage over the scored window. The old value states the correct, sourced boundary: the effect is a function of bounded active-seconds supplied by the scenario, and mere item presence implies zero stasis seconds.
